rationale: C20 is an unmistakable drafting predecessor: it has the same title subject and reproduces the same three-item sequence of statutory provisions governing the appointments, with nearly verbatim citations and ordering. The child appears to continue or update the same operative arrangement and adds a new effective date. C07 is also closely related and contains the identical statutory list, but C20 is stronger because it is the immediately preceding Eisenhower order and expressly continues the appointments through July 1, 1953, directly anticipating the child's July 1, 1953 effective date. C06 shares only the generic device of enumerating three statutes and does not address the same appointments or laws.

shared_material.child_excerpt: 1. Sections 37 and 38 of the act of June 3, 1916 ... and section 127a of that act as added by the act of June 4, 1920 ...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: 1. Sections 37 and 38 of the act of June 3, 1916 ... and section 127a of that act as added by the act of June 4, 1920 ...
shared_material.explanation: The first statutory item is substantively identical and occupies the same position.

shared_material.child_excerpt: 2. Section 515 (e) of the act of August 7, 1947 ... 3. Section 3 of the act of August 21, 1941 ...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: 2. Section 515 (e) of the act of August 7, 1947 ... 3. Section 3 of the act of August 21, 1941 ...
shared_material.explanation: The second and third statutory items are repeated in the same order with essentially identical citations.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This order shall become effective on July 1, 1953.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hereby continue in effect until and including July 1, 1953, all appointments as officers and as warrant officers ...
shared_material.explanation: The child's effective date aligns directly with the endpoint established by C20, supporting a continuation or replacement relationship rather than coincidental shared language.
